MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Friendly and dynamic team

Flexible working arrangements

Permanent part time, 2 days per week

About the Role
You will support initiatives aimed to enhance compliance with clinical and administrative activities linked with activity-based funding.

You will provide support and training across the program in relation to clinical data and its use to inform clinical care, and service activity data to comply with legislative and other reporting requirements.

Support initiatives to enhance compliance with activities linked to activity-based funding (Phase of Care, outcome measures, diagnoses, contact data entry, consumer registrations) and the achievement of service hours activity targets across the program

Facilitate education and training in information systems and processes across multiple staffing groups

Support managers, clinical and non-clinical staff in accessing and interpreting relevant data relating to clinical care and administrative processes

Support specified continuous quality improvement initiatives, including clinical auditing and the development of resources to support staff in relevant activities

The classification for this position will be YC89 - AK17 ($74,438 - $83,279 per annum pro rata)

Your Contribution 

High level interpersonal skills, including the ability to engage and motivate staff in processes relevant to health information

Proven communication, organisational, decision making and problem-solving abilities

Understanding of mental health and hospital information systems, policies and standards related to mental health (highly desirable)

Demonstrated ability to navigate the Client Management Interface (CMI) mental health database (highly desirable)

Proficient in Microsoft Office and other packages necessary to collect, collate and conduct basic research and generate statistics

Current National criminal history check, or willing to obtain

What We Offer

A focus on wellbeing initiatives, with regular events and programs

Confidential, solutions-focused employee counselling

A healthy work-life balance encouraged.

Ability to join Fitness Passport - Your pass to an extensive choice of fitness facilities

Salary Packaging - Increase your take home pay!

Regular opportunities for professional development to assist you to reach your career goals

Culture of continuous improvement

About the Mental Health Team
This position is located within the Mental Health Service Development Unit, reporting to the Manager.

The position collaborates closely with both the SVHM Health Information Services team and the Decision Support Unit. The role is located across sites including Fitzroy, East Melbourne, Kew and Hawthorn.

Working at St Vincent's 
St Vincent's Hospital Melbourne (SVHM) is a leading teaching, research and tertiary health service. SVHM provides a diverse range of adult clinical services and is driven by values of Compassion, Justice, Integrity and Excellence.

Application

Please attach your resume and cover letter to your application.

Shortlisting for this position will commence immediately. We encourage you to apply promptly as the advertisement may close early should a suitable applicant be sourced.

We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and abilities. Inclusion is essential to our mission and diversity reflects the community we serve.

Please visit our website, for further information regarding our Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Employment at SVHM

SVHA has a duty of care under work health and safety legislation to eliminate and-or control the risk of transmission of vaccine preventable diseases in healthcare settings. You may therefore be required to undergo mandatory immunisations-vaccinations

Payroll Officer – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $75,000 – $90,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Payroll Officer to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Payroll Officer, you will be responsible for managing payroll processing activities, maintaining accurate employee records, and ensuring employees are paid correctly and on time. You will work closely with the finance, human resources, project, and operational teams to ensure payroll processes comply with company policies, awards, employment conditions, and relevant legislation.

Key Responsibilities
•	Process end-to-end payroll activities for employees, including weekly and fortnightly payroll cycles.
•	Maintain accurate employee payroll records, including salaries, allowances, deductions, leave balances, and employment details.
•	Verify timesheets, overtime, allowances, leave applications, and payroll adjustments.
•	Ensure payroll calculations comply with relevant awards, enterprise agreements, employment contracts, and legislation.
•	Process new employee onboarding, payroll setup, and employee changes.
•	Manage employee queries relating to payroll, leave entitlements, deductions, and payments.
•	Prepare payroll reports, reconciliations, and supporting documentation for management and finance teams.
•	Process superannuation payments, payroll tax, PAYG withholding, and other statutory obligations.
•	Maintain accurate records and assist with payroll audits and compliance reviews.
•	Liaise with HR, project managers, supervisors, and employees regarding payroll-related matters.
•	Assist with improving payroll processes and maintaining payroll system accuracy.
•	Ensure confidentiality and security of employee payroll information.
•	Follow workplace health and safety policies, company procedures, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Payroll Officer or in a similar payroll/finance administration role.
•	Experience processing payroll in a medium to large organisation is highly regarded.
•	Strong understanding of payroll processes, employment conditions, and statutory requirements.
•	Experience with payroll software and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
•	Strong attention to detail and accuracy in handling financial and employee data.
•	Excellent organisational and time management skills.
•	Ability to manage confidential information professionally.
•	Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively with employees and management teams.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $75,000 – $90,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work within a growing mining and industrial services organisation.
•	Ongoing training and professional development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

About the role:

We've currently looking for a motivated Health Information Clerk to join our busy team at St Vincent's Private Hospital Northside on a casual basis. This is a great opportunity for a detailed-orientated clerk to provide timely administrative support, while ensuring compliance, privacy and confidentiality. 

Some of the key responsibilities in this role could include:

Preparing, retrieving, preparing and archiving patient medical records

Scanning, uploading and maintaining patient medical records

Supporting clinicians throughout the hospital with timely access for medical records

Undertaking general administrative duties with the Health Informatics department

Things that work for you: 

Retail and Travel Discounts; Blue light card a discounted service for frontline workers (available for over 350 brands inc. Big W, The Good Guys, Samsung), JB Hi-Fi corporate benefits, airport lounge membership discounts

Financial Wellbeing: Salary packaging options up to $15,990, novated leasing, plus an optional Meals and Entertainment card up to $2,650 per annum, competitive hourly rates and paid approved overtime

Health and Wellbeing: Employee Assistance Program for staff and their families, fitness passport, free uniforms & annual flu vaccination, ability to purchase annual leave, discounted hospital admissions at any St Vincent's Private Hospital, discounted private health insurance through Bupa or Medibank

Join Australia's largest not-for-profit provider of health and aged care services

Previous experience in a medical records, health information services or healthcare administration is highly desirable

Strong attention to detail with

Previous experience in perioperative or acute care (desirable but not essential)

Our hospital has 227 beds, 9 operating theatres, 2 cardiac catheter laboratories, a 17-bed Intensive Care Unit (ICU), Day Oncology Unit, Breast Health Centre, Endoscopy Unit, Cardiac Rehabilitation Unit and a 24-hour, private emergency centre provided by Brisbane Northside Emergency.

## Network Administrator
## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and proactive Network Administrator to join our team and play a key role in maintaining the integrity, performance, and security of our organisation's network infrastructure. The ideal candidate will bring hands-on experience in network administration, a methodical approach to troubleshooting, and the ability to communicate technical concepts clearly across all levels of the business. This role suits a detail-oriented professional who thrives in a dynamic environment and is committed to delivering reliable, efficient IT services.
## Key Responsibilities
- Install, configure, and maintain network hardware, software, servers, and workstations, ensuring systems are kept up to date and performing optimally
- Monitor network performance on an ongoing basis, identifying and resolving issues proactively to minimise disruption to business operations
- Diagnose and troubleshoot network faults, emergencies, and connectivity issues, documenting resolutions and maintaining accurate records of all incidents and modifications
- Develop, maintain, and update procedures and documentation for network inventory, configuration changes, and maintenance instructions
- Manage user accounts, access permissions, and password policies in line with the organisation's security standards and compliance requirements
- Provide network programming and scripting support to address specific business needs and improve the efficiency of network operations
- Administer and support servers, printers, and personal computers, ensuring hardware resources remain reliable and fit for purpose
- Evaluate and implement upgrades to network infrastructure, recommending improvements that align with business growth and evolving technology requirements
- Deliver helpdesk support and technical assistance to end users, resolving issues in a timely manner and escalating complex problems where necessary
- Conduct user training and produce clear guidance materials to build internal capability and promote best practice use of network systems
- Maintain network security protocols, including firewall management, intrusion detection, and vulnerability assessments, to safeguard organisational data and systems
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders and external vendors to coordinate service delivery, procurement, and project implementation
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree or diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, Network Engineering, or a related discipline
- Proven experience in a network administration or systems administration role within a corporate or enterprise environment
- Strong working knowledge of networking protocols, infrastructure components, and technologies including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, LAN/WAN, and firewalls
- Demonstrated experience installing, configuring, and managing servers, switches, routers, and associated network hardware
- Proficiency in network monitoring and diagnostic tools, with the ability to analyse performance data and respond to anomalies
- Solid understanding of network security principles, including access control, patch management, and risk mitigation
- Experience maintaining technical documentation, network inventories, and fault resolution records to a high standard
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work methodically under pressure
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to explain technical issues to non-technical stakeholders
- Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, and contribute effectively within a collaborative team environment
## Preferred Qualifications
- Industry certifications such as Cisco CCNA/CCNP, CompTIA Network+, Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator, or equivalent
- Experience with virtualisation platforms such as VMware or Hyper-V
- Familiarity with cloud-based infrastructure and hybrid network environments
- Experience working within ITIL frameworks or other structured IT service management methodologies
- Exposure to scripting or automation tools such as PowerShell, Python, or Ansible to streamline network operations
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a supportive, forward-thinking team that values continuous learning and invests in your professional development through training and certification opportunities
- Enjoy genuine flexibility with a structured work schedule that promotes a healthy work-life balance
- Work on diverse and challenging infrastructure projects that will broaden your technical expertise and keep your skills at the cutting edge
- Join an organisation with a strong culture of collaboration, where your contributions are recognised and your ideas are encouraged
- Competitive remuneration package with long-term career pathways and opportunities for progression within a growing business
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation
